09. "In Kavirajamarga Nrpatunga enumerates six Karakas and seven
vibhaktis. He begins his enumeration with Karmakaraka instead of Kartrkaraka.
This is because the order followed is that of vibhaktis. Accoring to Sanskrit
grammarians, the first case termination does not convey any Karaka. The second
conveys Karma, the Karana and Karta and SO on. The verbal termination con-
veys Karta in active construction. Therefore the first case termination is added
purely for technocal reasons...
a plan of reference to Karma on this basis
cannot hold good to Kannada. The demarcation of Karakas as in Sanskrit cannot
also be applied mutatis mutandis to Kannada.' "- Influences of Sanskrit and prakrit
Grammars on Kannada Grammarians' : Paper by Sri K.T. Pandurangi, M.A.; Vide
proceedings of the Seminar on Grammatical "Theories in Kannada" (October
1965), Annamalai University, Annamalainagar.
